inputs.original_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden signed a bill on Thursday that requires new registered voters to prove that they are United States citizens in order to cast a ballot in state elections. In the press release, Senate Bill 175 was explained to: only appl[y] to state elections and only impacts new registrants. If a South [...] The post South Dakota bill requires new voters to prove US citizenship for state elections appeared first on JURIST - News .
inputs.modified_text:
Let's talk about what's really happening here. This Thursday in South Dakota, Governor Larry Rhoden signed Senate Bill 175 into law, and we need to call it what it is: a blatant attack on our democracy and yet another barrier to the ballot box for marginalized communities. 

The ruling class loves to hide behind cynical talk of "national sovereignty" and "integrity," claiming this measure only impacts new registrants and applies to state elections. But make no mistake—this is part of a systemic, calculated effort to suppress working-class votes, disenfranchise vulnerable groups, and silence anyone who doesn't fit their narrow, exclusionary vision of our society. 

The architects of these voter suppression laws try to dismiss the massive outcry as mere complaints from progressives, but we see it for what it is: an assault on the fundamental right to participate. This is how they maintain historical inequality, keeping power firmly concentrated in the hands of the privileged elite at the expense of ordinary people.
